RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Avery Jennings
Member ID: W675944637
Reference Number: POC-CDC085AB1F-87245
Date of Notice: 2026-08-22
Requested Service: Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
Treating Surgeon: Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29827 (arthroscopic rotator cuff repair), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-22 (Reference No. POC-CDC085AB1F-87245). This appeal is submitted within the 180-day window stated in that notice (deadline 2027-02-18).

Stated Reason for Denial

The notice states that the request was denied because "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal together with the clinical records identified below, which I believe directly address each element the plan requires to evaluate medical necessity for this procedure.

Note on Policy Quotation

I have identified the medical policy that Regence uses to evaluate rotator cuff repair as Medical Policy Manual, Surgery, Policy No. 228, "Shoulder Surgeries" (SUR228). Below, wherever I quote the policy's criteria, the quoted language is text I retrieved directly from that policy document. I have not been able to confirm from the notice itself, or from my plan documents, that this is the exact policy version and criteria set applied to my specific claim; I am requesting that the plan confirm this or provide the specific criteria actually used, per my request below.

Mapping of Clinical Records to Policy Criteria

The policy states: "Rotator cuff repair may be considered medically necessary when all of the following Criteria are met (A.-D.):"

A. "Documentation of function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living and/or demands of employment)"

- My records document 12 months of progressive shoulder pain, unrelieved by rest, and note that I "cannot lift the arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side." This is a direct, ongoing interference with activities of daily living.

B. The policy requires either (1) "Failure to respond to at least three months of non-surgical management which includes documentation of physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program and one or more of the following unless contraindicated: a. Trial of anti-inflammatory medication; or b. Cortisone injection" or (2) an acute traumatic tear meeting separate criteria.

- My records satisfy criterion B.1.: I completed 16 weeks (2026-04-06 to 2026-07-27, 18 visits) of supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note — well in excess of the three-month minimum.
- In addition, I completed a 6-month trial of NSAIDs with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-27, which provided only 3 weeks of partial relief. Both the anti-inflammatory medication trial and the cortisone injection referenced in criterion B.1.a. and B.1.b. are therefore documented.

C. The policy requires, on physical examination compared to the non-involved side: "1. Either of the following: a. Functionally limited active range of motion; or b. Measurable loss of strength of the rotator cuff musculature; and 2. One or more of the following positive orthopedic tests/signs" (the policy lists the Drop Arm Test, Painful Arc Test, Jobe or Empty Can Test, External Rotation Lag Sign, Internal Rotation Lag Sign, Lift-Off Test, Bear Hug Test, Belly-Press Test, Belly-Off Test, Neer Impingement Test, Hawkins-Kennedy Impingement, and Hornblower Test among the accepted findings).

- My exam findings, as documented by Dr. Reyes, show range of motion "limited by pain" and "positive provocative testing on the affected side." [The specific named orthopedic test(s) performed and the specific strength deficit measurement are not contained in the clinical summary provided to me; I have asked Dr. Reyes's office to supply the exact test names and any measured strength/range-of-motion deficits so the record explicitly matches the policy's enumerated tests in C.2.]

D. "Advanced diagnostic imaging study (e.g., MRI, CT) demonstrates a partial-thickness rotator cuff tear or a full-thickness rotator cuff tear that correlates with the individual's reported symptoms and physical exam findings."

- The MRI performed 2026-06-30 documents a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy. This finding directly correlates with my 12-month history of function-limiting pain, inability to lift the arm above shoulder height, and the positive examination findings noted by my surgeon.

Additional Relevant Information

- I have no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder.
- My BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.
- [Any additional comorbidity, employment-function, or activity-limitation detail the plan requires — not contained in the records provided to me.]

Enclosures

1. Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-06 to 2026-07-27, 18 visits)
2. Medication trial records / NSAID history (approx. 6 months)
3. Corticosteroid injection record dated 2026-05-27
4. MRI report dated 2026-06-30
5. Office/exam notes from Dr. Reyes documenting function-limiting pain, range-of-motion limitation, and positive provocative testing
6. [Any additional records the plan specifically identified as missing — not described in the notice provided to me]

Request

Because the stated basis for denial was incomplete documentation rather than a finding that the clinical criteria were not met, I ask that the plan re-review this request in light of the enclosed records against the criteria in Medical Policy SUR228, "Shoulder Surgeries." If any specific item is still considered missing, I ask that the plan identify exactly which criterion (A, B, C, or D) or sub-element is unmet so that I or Dr. Reyes's office can supply the precise missing documentation before or during this appeal.

I also request, per my right to receive the specific rules, guidelines, or clinical review criteria relied upon in this determination, written confirmation of:
(a) the exact version/effective date of the medical policy applied to my claim, and
(b) any additional internal review criteria (e.g., clinical review guidelines) used beyond the policy criteria quoted above.

Please notify me and Dr. Reyes's office of the outcome of this appeal in writing. If any information above requires clarification, you may contact me at [phone/email — not contained in the records] or Dr. Reyes's office at [office contact — not contained in the records].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Avery Jennings
